I'd suggest making it a static bool so we only test this once per session, to avoid redoing such test all the time.

Actually, the whole function should likely be called only once and saved in a static bool. It's called in `LightmapGI::get_configuration_warnings` so any time a scene with a LightmapGI is refreshed, it would call this. Even outside the Windows/Nvidia issue, creating RenderingContextDrivers all the time doesn't sound like a great idea for performance/memory usage.
`created_rendering_device` is static variable (3 state), it's already checking it once.
Oh right I missed this. Looks good then.
This is already saving the results in `created_rendering_device`, so nevermind.
This causes unreachable code error, will write a fix (Seems we need more fine-grained testing for Windows builds as this is the second regression in a short bit)
